body:
Thank you for this report. It is the best data that we have on this fault. Answers to your three questions, and one request.

## 1. Do we see it, and do we know the cause?
Yes, we see it. We do not know the cause.
- Linux runner `uma`, post-merge run 45046106061 (commit 87fb95f29): `ui suites: lib` ended with SIGSEGV 4 seconds after its start. Other runs of the same runner are green.
- A Windows machine here: `0xc0000005` one time, 5 seconds after `running 1464 tests`. After that, 150 starts of the binary gave no crash (NVIDIA / software adapter, not Intel).
- Our issue for it was #3548. I close #3548 as a duplicate of this issue, because your data is better: a rate of about one half, the condition "more than one test thread", and the adapter.
- What we know from the code: 87fb95f29 is the first commit in which `camcraft-ui` links `camcraft-gpu` and `wgpu`. Three lib tests that are not ignored make GPU objects, each with its own instance: `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds` (the headless start path of the product), `egui_app::report_tests::a_kind_button_asks_the_shell_for_the_whole_window` (a test renderer that lists the adapters of each backend) and `egui_app::gpu::tests::adapter_probe_names_the_gpu`. The hypothesis, not proved: a race when these make or drop a `wgpu` instance or a device at the same time, in the driver or in a backend. Your result with one test thread (6 of 6 green) agrees with it.

## 2. A pull request while the fault exists
Your plan is correct, and it is what we do: if `ui suites: lib` ends with `0xc0000005` or a signal, with no FAILED test and no panic text, run that one step again, two more times at most. Write in the PR body that the crash of this issue came (name #3589) and give the count of the green run, and the pinning tests by name. A reviewer does not count that crash against the PR. A failure with a test name is a real failure.

## 3. A crash dump
If you can use administrator rights one time: the registry key `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\LocalDumps`, with the values `DumpFolder` (REG_EXPAND_SZ, a folder of your choice), `DumpType` (REG_DWORD) = 2 and `DumpCount` = 5. It applies to each program. Remove the key after the test. Do not attach the dump here (it can hold private data): the stack of the crashed thread is sufficient.

## The request (no administrator rights are necessary)
Windows writes the faulting module for each crash. In PowerShell:

```
Get-WinEvent -LogName Application -MaxEvents 200 | Where-Object { $_.Id -eq 1000 -and $_.Message -match 'camcraft_ui' } | Select-Object -First 3 -ExpandProperty Message
```

The lines "Faulting module name" and "Exception offset" tell us if the crash is in the Intel driver (`ig*.dll`), in `vulkan-1.dll` / `d3d12` / `opengl32`, or in our binary. With your rate, two more runs help much:
- `$env:CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE='off'`, then the lib tests 6 times with the default threads;
- the three tests above only, 20 times: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- headless_run_succeeds a_kind_button_asks_the_shell adapter_probe_names_the_gpu --test-threads=16`.

We make a change that lets these tests use the GPU one at a time (one lock, or one shared instance for the test process). When its branch is pushed, a run on your machine is the proof that we cannot get here.

## The build cache observation
"found invalid metadata files" with 16 jobs is a different fault. Please open an issue for it with the four error lines; say if `sccache` is in use (`RUSTC_WRAPPER`).

An early answer to the safety question: can the shipped app crash at the same place? From a read of the code on `main` (60376ccbb); nothing was run.

**No, as far as the read shows. The priority stays `P2`.**
- The desktop app makes one `wgpu` instance, one adapter and one device, on the UI thread (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/gpu_init.rs:57`, from `shell_window.rs:247`). A second instance comes only when an earlier backend attempt fails, and those attempts are one after the other.
- The headless start makes one instance (`crates/gpu/src/adapter.rs:76`, from `shell.rs:1094`).
- `camcraft-cli` and the MCP server have no `wgpu` dependency.
- The shared compute device (`crates/gpu/src/shared.rs:20`) and the cut kernel (`cut_run.rs:50`) have no caller outside `camcraft-gpu` and its tests. The app does not use them yet.
- So no path of the product has two GPU objects at the same time, and none touches the GPU from two threads.

**The test binary is different.** Seven lib tests touch the GPU, not three: `headless_run_succeeds`, `adapter_probe_names_the_gpu`, `a_kind_button_asks_the_shell_for_the_whole_window`, and four more tests in `report_tests.rs` that click "Report a bug" (the screenshot command makes a test renderer on the next step). With the default test threads, up to seven instances can be alive at the same time. On Windows the default backend mask contains GL, and each GL instance starts its own thread with a hidden window (`wgpu-hal` 30.0.1, `gles/wgl.rs:372-392`). That this is the cause is a guess, not a fact.

**What follows**
- The fix under way: one test-only lock that the seven tests hold while they make and use the GPU (held across the step in which the renderer is made).
- A note for the work on #2629 (the viewport that will use the compute device): when the app gets a second device, this fault can come to the product. That slice must use the render device, or make and drop the second device on the same thread with no overlap. I record it there.
- If your event log names the faulting module, it decides between the guess above and a different cause.

claimed: issue-worker-high #3589 (Opus) · 2026-11-23T01:38Z · worktree/branch issue/3589-gpu-test-lock · plan: one test-only lock so the seven GPU lib tests of camcraft-ui use the GPU one at a time, with a pin test.

Results of the requests, from the Windows 11 machine of this report (Intel Arc B390 and the Microsoft WARP software adapter, 16 logical CPUs, rustc 1.99.1, debug profile). All runs are on `main` commit 4c0a157e1. I ran the lib test binary that `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` builds (`target\debug\deps\camcraft_ui-<hash>.exe`) directly, from `crates\ui`, with the same arguments. A run "crashed" when the process ended with exit code 0xc0000005 and wrote no `test result` line.

## 1. Event log
I ran your command. It returned 25 events for `camcraft_ui` (event 1000). They are all my crashes from the last two hours, on `main` and on the branches of two small pull requests. All 25 have exception code 0xc0000005 and the faulting module `d3d10warp.dll`, version 10.0.26100.9818. No event names the Intel driver, `vulkan-1.dll`, `opengl32` or our binary.

Fault offsets in `d3d10warp.dll`:

| Offset | Events |
|---|---|
| 0xa89b3 | 15 |
| 0x7b3b4 | 5 |
| 0x7b40d | 2 |
| 0x7b459 | 1 |
| 0xa7959 | 1 |
| 0xa790c | 1 |

CamCraft's log names this adapter as "Microsoft Basic Render Driver ... cpu via dx12".

## 2. `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`, whole lib suite, default threads
- With `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`: 6 runs, 1 crashed (after 285 tests), 5 passed (1475 tests each).
- Without the variable, same method, 8 runs: 2 crashed, 6 passed.
- Earlier, with `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` on `main`: 8 of 15 crashed.

I see no difference between "off" and the default.

## 3. The GPU tests, 20 runs each, `--test-threads=16`
- Your three tests, with your filters (`headless_run_succeeds a_kind_button_asks_the_shell adapter_probe_names_the_gpu --test-threads=16`): 20 runs, 0 crashes.
- Seven tests, in one command, with `--test-threads=16`: 20 runs, 4 crashed, 16 passed (7 tests each).

The seven are:
1. `headless_run_succeeds`
2. `adapter_probe_names_the_gpu`
3. `a_kind_button_asks_the_shell_for_the_whole_window`
4. `the_title_field_travels_into_the_url`
5. `the_answer_copies_the_picture_and_says_the_word`
6. `the_picture_is_still_copied_after_the_window_is_closed`
7. `no_answer_copies_nothing`

How I chose tests 4 to 7: your second comment names three tests and says "four more tests in `report_tests.rs` that click Report a bug". In `crates/ui/src/egui_app/report_tests.rs`, five tests click the button with the label "Report a bug": `a_kind_button_asks_the_shell_for_the_whole_window` (named by you) and the four tests above. This is my reading of the code. It is not confirmed. `the_door_opens_the_window_and_a_kind_button_files_the_url` clicks "Request a feature", not "Report a bug". I did not include it.

In each of the 4 crashed runs, at least one of the five "Report a bug" tests (tests 3 to 7) had not finished when the process ended. I read this from the output: a test with no `... ok` line yet. The tests not finished in each crashed run:
- Run 11: `a_kind_button_asks_the_shell_for_the_whole_window`
- Run 12: six of the seven, including `headless_run_succeeds` and all five "Report a bug" tests (only `adapter_probe_names_the_gpu` had printed its result)
- Run 13: `the_picture_is_still_copied_after_the_window_is_closed`
- Run 18: `the_title_field_travels_into_the_url`

In runs 11, 13 and 18, `headless_run_succeeds` and `adapter_probe_names_the_gpu` had both finished when the process ended.

## Not done
- No crash dump: I did not make the registry change.
- I did not run your lock branch. I will run it when it is pushed, if you want.

A correction to my statement of 2026-11-23 that no path of the product touches the GPU from two threads.

That is true on `main` today. PR #3585 (open, not merged) changes it: a worker thread makes the pipelines of the stock eye on the same device, while the UI thread draws the first frames. This is one instance and one device, so it is not the case that this issue suspects (two or more instances or devices at the same time). wgpu permits it. I record it here so that the analysis of this issue has the correct facts after #3585 merges.

fix on issue/3589-gpu-test-lock · PR #3604 · pinned by egui_app::gpu_test_lock::every_gpu_test_takes_the_lock, egui_app::gpu_test_lock::the_lock_lets_one_holder_in_at_a_time, egui_app::gpu_test_lock::a_panic_with_the_lock_held_does_not_block_the_next_test · merges when reviewed

The PR changes test code only. The eight `camcraft-ui` lib tests that make a wgpu instance now use the GPU one at a time. The issue stays open until the reporter confirms the result.

@brenmarshall, please do a test of the branch on your Windows 11 machine:

1. Get the branch: `git fetch origin` and `git switch issue/3589-gpu-test-lock`.
2. Run `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` 20 times, with the default number of test threads.
3. Report the result of each run here: passed, failed, or `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION`.
4. If a run stops, give the name of the last test in the output.

PR #3604 is merged (`0839e979e`). It is test code only: the eight `camcraft-ui` lib tests that start a GPU renderer now use the GPU one at a time. The `in-review` label is removed because no PR is open. This issue stays open. @brenmarshall: please run `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` 20 times on `main` at `0839e979e` or later, and tell us the number of runs that end with `0xc0000005`.

Result of the check of the lock fix (PR #3604): **0 of 20 runs ended with 0xc0000005.**

Commit tested: `main` at `f35202134`. It contains `0839e979e` (the merge of PR #3604) and the lock commit `67f7fe1e1`. I checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor 0839e979e HEAD`.

How I ran it (the same machine as before: Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, 16 logical CPUs, Intel Arc B390 and the WARP adapter, rustc 1.99.1, debug profile):
- One build: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib --no-run`.
- Then `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, 20 times, one run after the other, with the default number of test threads. Nothing else was running on the machine. The runs lasted from 02:57Z to 03:14Z.

Outcome of each run:
- Runs 1 to 20: passed, each with 1485 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored. The cargo exit code was 0 each time.
- No run stopped early, so there is no "last test" to name.
- Runs with 0xc0000005: 0.

Event log: no new Application event 1000 for `camcraft_ui` since the start of the runs (earlier today the same log held 25 such events from my crashes before the fix).

For comparison, before the fix on `main` at 4c0a157e1, the same test binary ended with 0xc0000005 in 8 of 15 runs (`cargo test`) and in 2 of 8 runs (started directly). 20 runs cannot show that the crash is gone. In my earlier runs with the default threads, the longest run of clean results was 4.

I did not run the seven-test subset again.

The reporter confirms the fix: 0 of 20 runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` end with `0xc0000005` on `main` at `f35202134`, which has the test lock of PR #3604 (merge `0839e979e`, commit `67f7fe1e1`). Thank you for the careful check. The work is done by that commit, so this issue closes. Open follow-up: #3605 (two integration test binaries and three ignored tests still make a GPU device with no lock). If the fault comes back, reopen this issue with the run output.
